books.title: The Possessed
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.desc: In a Russian provincial town, a circle of young revolutionaries gathers around a mysterious aristocrat, and their plotting ends in murder.
about: In a provincial town, the ageing liberal idealist Stepan Trofimovitch Verhovensky lives under the protection of the wealthy Varvara Petrovna, whose son, Nikolay Stavrogin, returns home after years of scandals. Soon Stepan Trofimovitch's son, Pyotr Verhovensky, arrives and gathers a small circle of radicals, among them the engineer Kirillov, obsessed with the idea of suicide, and the former student Shatov, who wants to leave the group. As Pyotr's schemes spread disorder through the town, the conspiracy moves towards violence.

Dostoevsky's novel is at once a political satire, a tragedy and a philosophical drama about faith, nihilism, freedom and the moral consequences of revolutionary ideas. Its gallery of characters, from the enigmatic Stavrogin to the crippled Marya Timofyevna and the drunken Captain Lebyadkin, mixes grotesque comedy and horror.

The novel was published in The Russian Messenger in 1871 and 1872. Dostoevsky drew on the murder in 1869 of the student Ivan Ivanov by members of the revolutionary group of Sergey Nechayev. Also known in English as Demons, it is offered here in Constance Garnett's English translation (1916) and Victor Derély's French translation (1886).

books.title: First Love and Other Stories
books.author: Ivan Turgenev
books.desc: One summer in the country, sixteen-year-old Vladímir falls in love with Zinaída, the bewitching older girl next door, and discovers she has a secret.
about: In the title story, a middle-aged man, Vladímir Petróvitch, recalls the summer when he was sixteen and his family rented a country house near Moscow. In the shabby wing next door lived the impoverished Princess Zasyékin and her daughter Zinaída, a capricious and fascinating young woman of twenty-one who amused herself with a circle of admirers. Vladímir falls hopelessly in love with her, until he begins to suspect that she loves someone else. The volume also contains the stories "A Correspondence", "The Region of Dead Calm", "It Is Enough" and "The Dog".
Turgenev's novella is a delicate study of adolescent passion, jealousy and disillusion, and of a son's complicated relationship with his father, told with restraint and melancholy.

First Love was published in March 1860. Turgenev described it as the most autobiographical of his works, drawn from his own youthful infatuation with a neighbour. The English translation is by Isabel F. Hapgood, from her edition of Turgenev's novels and stories.

books.title: Beyond Good and Evil
books.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
books.desc: Nietzsche attacks the hidden assumptions of past philosophers and of conventional morality, and calls for free spirits who will create new values.
about: Subtitled "Prelude to a Philosophy of the Future", the book is divided into nine parts made up of 296 numbered sections, ending with a poem. Nietzsche begins with "the prejudices of philosophers", questioning their faith in truth and in opposite values, then turns to the "free spirit", religion, morality, the scholar, the virtues, peoples and nations, and finally to the question "What is noble?".

In short, often aphoristic passages, Nietzsche criticises dogmatism and the morality he sees in Christianity and in modern democratic ideas, and develops ideas such as the will to power and the distinction between "master" and "slave" morality. Some passages contain generalisations about women and peoples that reflect prejudices of its time.

Beyond Good and Evil was published in 1886 by C. G. Naumann in Leipzig, at the author's own expense. This edition offers the German original and the English translation by Helen Zimmern, first published in 1907.

books.title: The Robbers
books.author: Friedrich Schiller
books.desc: Disinherited through his brother's scheming, a young nobleman becomes the leader of a band of outlaws in the Bohemian forests.
about: Count Maximilian von Moor has two sons: Karl, generous and impetuous, who is away from home, and the younger Franz, cold and envious. Franz uses a false letter to convince their father that Karl is a criminal, and the old count disowns his elder son. In despair, Karl becomes the captain of a band of robbers, among them Spiegelberg, Schweitzer and Kosinsky, while at home Franz schemes to seize the inheritance and to win Karl's beloved, Amalia. In the English translation the brothers are called Charles and Francis, and Amalia is Amelia.
Schiller's first play is a passionate drama of rebellion, freedom and justice, a key work of the Sturm und Drang movement, contrasting the noble outlaw Karl with his calculating brother.

The Robbers was published almost anonymously in 1781 and first performed on 13 January 1782 at the National Theatre in Mannheim, where its success made the young author famous. This edition offers the German original and an anonymous English translation.
books.author_short: German poet, playwright, historian and philosopher (1759–1805), author of The Robbers, Mary Stuart and William Tell.
author_long: Friedrich Schiller was born on 10 November 1759 in Marbach am Neckar, in the Duchy of Württemberg. Educated at a military academy in Stuttgart, he studied medicine and worked as a regimental doctor before devoting himself to writing. From 1788 he formed a close friendship with Goethe, which shaped the period known as Weimar Classicism. He died in Weimar on 9 May 1805.
His plays include The Robbers (1781), the Wallenstein trilogy (1800–1801), Mary Stuart (1801) and William Tell (1804). His poem "Ode to Joy" inspired the choral finale of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony.

books.title: In Search of the Castaways
books.author: Jules Verne
books.desc: A message in a bottle sends a Scottish lord, his wife and the children of a missing captain around the world along the 37th parallel.
about: Lord Glenarvan, a Scottish laird, finds a bottle inside a shark caught by his yacht, the Duncan. Its damaged messages, in English, French and German, reveal that Captain Harry Grant and two of his sailors were shipwrecked on the 37th parallel south. Moved by Grant's children, Mary and Robert, Glenarvan and his wife Helena set out to find him, accompanied by Major McNabbs, Captain John Mangles and the absent-minded French geographer Paganel, who boards the Duncan by mistake. Their search takes them across South America, Australia and New Zealand.

Verne's adventure novel combines geography, natural history, humour and suspense. Its descriptions of the indigenous peoples of South America, Australia and New Zealand, often called "savages", reflect the colonial views of its time.

Les Enfants du capitaine Grant was published in serial form in 1867 and 1868 in Hetzel's Magasin d'éducation et de récréation, in three parts entitled South America, Australia and New Zealand. This edition offers the French original and an anonymous English translation.
